results.name: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press
instructions: Lie back on a decline bench with your feet firmly planted. Hold a dumbbell in each hand close together above your chest using a neutral grip.
Bend your elbows and lower the dumbbells toward your chest while keeping your palms facing each other and your elbows close to your torso.
Press both dumbbells upward together until your arms are extended directly above your chest without locking your elbows.
Slowly lower the dumbbells along the same path until they return close to your chest, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows tucked close to your torso as you lower the weights.
Press the dumbbells directly above your chest without letting them drift toward your head.
Maintain contact between your head, back, hips, and the bench throughout the exercise.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Close Neutral Grip Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline Fly
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured and holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended straight out to your sides at chest level with palms facing up.
Raise the dumbbells up in a wide arc until your arms are straight above your chest, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back out to the sides in a controlled motion, keeping the slight bend in your elbows, until your arms are level with your chest.
Repeat the steps for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Exhale as you raise the dumbbells and inhale as you lower them.
Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline Hammer Press
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured and holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms bent and dumbbells by your sides with palms facing each other.
Raise the dumbbells up over your chest, extending your arms fully without locking your elbows, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position by your sides in a controlled motion.
Repeat the steps for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Hammer Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline One Arm Hammer Press
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured, holding a dumbbell in one hand with your arm bent and the dumbbell by your side, palm facing inward. Place your other hand on the bench for stability.
Raise the dumbbell up over your chest, extending your arm fully without locking your elbow, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position by your side in a controlled motion.
Repeat the steps for the desired number of repetitions, then switch arms and repeat.
tips: Exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Hold the bench tightly with your free hand to ensure proper balance.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline One Arm Hammer Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline Twist Fly
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured and holding a dumbbell in each hand. Extend your arms straight out to your sides at chest level with palms facing each up.
As you raise the dumbbells up in a wide arc, twist your wrists so that your palms face backward, bringing the dumbbells to meet above your chest while maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower your arms back out to the sides in a controlled motion, twisting your wrists back so that your palms face up, until your arms are level with your chest.
Repeat the raising and lowering motion for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms during the twist.
Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Twist Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Floor Fly
instructions: Begin by lying on your back on the floor with your legs straight on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms slightly touch the floor.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
tips: Perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement.
Exhale as you lift the dumbbells back up and inhale as you lower them.
Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
results.description: Dumbbell Floor Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow
instructions: Begin by lying on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor for stability. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Slowly bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
results.description: Dumbbell Fly Flat Bench Slow is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Fly Incline Bench
instructions: Lie down on an incline bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand and lie back on the bench with your arms extended straight above your chest, palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbells out to your sides in a wide arc, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows. Lower until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below chest level.
Bring the dumbbells back up to the starting position by squeezing your chest muscles, keeping the slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.
tips: Avoid allowing the dumbbells to touch at the top to maintain tension in the chest muscles.
Keep your feet flat on the floor to provide stability and support.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Alternate Press
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set at a 45-degree angle, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms bent and dumbbells positioned near your chest.
Press the right dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended, keeping your palm facing forward.
Lower the right dumbbell back to the starting position with control while simultaneously starting to press the left dumbbell upward, maintaining proper form.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the press to protect your joints.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Alternate Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.
